new_leads.notes: Japanese and English item sources describe raised scaffolding along the avenue. Check the street-facing course first; nearby rooftop or scaffold loot is not proof of a specific Atlas Screw identity. Start at Café Gallant or Magenta Plaza Pokémon Center; exact ascent and relationship to screw 85 remain open.

new_leads.landmark: Alley west of eastern building complex
new_leads.notes: Search the scaffolding in the alley on the west side of the eastern building group. The reported screw is above ground; the approach is consistent with the existing Sector 2 scaffold clue, but the first climb has not been walked.

Find Chuckie and clear the Alpha Watchog blocking access in Side Mission 071. The owner's existing Lysandre Café/Autumnal Avenue photographed lift is a nearby candidate, NOT an identified mission device. Use the mission marker. Serebii places availability after the Rust Syndicate Office visit in MM24; Bulbapedia records completion of MM20. Gamepedia associates it with accepting MM24. Exact earliest trigger is unresolved.

A published screw route starts by Café Gallant, rises by Holovator and crosses the roof near benches and a bridge before descending into a narrow gap. This is a candidate connection from the existing Café Gallant lift photographs; exact turns, landing and pickup identity require visual comparison. Separately, the German area guide places TM009 on a triangular-building roof and records Hawluchanite as a mission reward; do not conflate a reward with a pickup.

new_leads.landmark: Magenta Plaza / Rogue Mega Altaria destination
new_leads.notes: The Japanese mission guide reports an ascent from the plaza edge followed by a counterclockwise rooftop approach in MM28. Roto-Glide may shorten the route. English location data places the boss on the central building roof. Compare the existing Magenta Plaza northwestern terrace lift ground and rooftop photos before identifying the exact entrance.

English route account describes entering the scaffold area by a battle court near Café Rouleau, ascending a ladder and descending from the roof onto a platform. Check which street entrance and roof edge are visible in the owner crop before writing precise turns. Source numbering differs from Atlas; no collectible match assumed.

Japanese route descriptions identify multiple reachable levels on the course; rolling is mentioned for crossing between platforms. The existing north-side clue pair 88/89 is consistent with lower and upper levels, but individual landings are not matched.

new_leads.landmark: South roof / west alley of large complex
new_leads.notes: English and Japanese sources place further rewards on the west-side scaffold and a smaller rooftop above the southern part of the building complex. Roto-Glide is reported for specific high-level pickups. Preserve separate candidate targets and verify the roof approach, rather than assuming all are reachable from the north course.

Japanese sources describe climbing from the northern courtyard and crossing toward a southern roof by Roto-Glide. Compare with the owner's sector reference near the sewer entrance. Existing roof clue 96 is a candidate; no exact building or ladder location assigned.

One English checklist points to a crate reached by rolling from an adjacent scaffold in the southwest alley. The location catalogue places a screw on scaffolding north of the southwestern complex; Japanese route notes also describe rolling between platforms. Compare the positions to determine whether these describe the same course and existing clue 95. Nearby canal lift is separate; no connection assumed.

new_leads.landmark: Southern building complex / Café Triste vicinity
new_leads.notes: Location catalogue describes access to a courtyard and southern/western roof pickups after clearing rock obstacles with Rock Smash. Some of this sector becomes Wild Zone 18 after MM30; early and late layouts need comparison. No specific lift, roof edge or screw identity assigned.

new_leads.landmark: Central gap and western North Boulevard edge
new_leads.notes: Existing screw clues distinguish a central course, two west-side platforms and a roof. Japanese summaries indicate multi-level obstacle courses; English area notes distinguish the central scaffolding from western roofing. Keep all four clues separate and verify access level and orientation; no direct connection assumed.

Japanese guides identify an interior scaffold platform for a Colorful Screw; English clue 91 also specifies the zone's scaffolding. Do not confuse it with platforms outside the zone between Zones 9 and 14. Need compare the two original Wild Zone photos and walk the entry-to-platform approach.

next_batch: Continue all remaining areas, prioritizing current G1 AT-320/AT-328 Bleu 7–10 reconciliation separately. Next unstarted district Rouge/Jaune, then Wild Zones; review existing Vert/Bleu research against additional language sources. No priority change to AT-325.
